items.title: How CFOs can make AI pay off
items.desc: Creating value from AI in finance—and beyond—requires setting measurable targets and redesigning processes. Here’s how.

items.title: Future of healthcare: Extinction or accelerated evolution?
items.desc: Shapers of healthcare’s future must evolve under relentless economic pressure. To avoid extinction, they must harness AI and biopharma breakthroughs to innovate clinical and business models.

items.title: Beyond agency boundaries: Building a statewide approach to customer experience
items.desc: As expectations for government evolve, three opportunities can help US states strengthen customer experience and service delivery to better meet residents’ needs.

items.title: How AI is transforming automotive quality operations
items.desc: Yoav Levy, cofounder and CEO of Upstream, explains how AI can reduce warranty and recall costs through early issue detection, accelerated investigations, and targeted countermeasures.

items.title: How AI can help unlock insurance growth in Latin America
items.desc: Latin America’s insurance market has strong growth and significant untapped demand. AI could help insurers reach even more customers and operate more efficiently.

items.title: Quality for quantity: The gains from investing in population health
items.desc: McKinsey Senior Partners Drew Ungerman and Pooja Kumar discuss the massive opportunities available to improve quality of life and economies by investing in three aspects of population health.

items.title: Reinventing the channel: How can your partner ecosystem fuel AI growth?
items.desc: AI presents an opportunity for technology vendors to reinvent their sales channels. This comprehensive overhaul would require five key moves.

items.title: The AI-enabled risk function of the future
items.desc: AI is reshaping how banks manage risk. The next challenge is scaling AI capabilities through a redesigned risk operating model.

items.title: From science fiction to reality: The next phase of shared autonomous mobility
items.desc: As shared autonomous vehicles expand into cities worldwide, operators are evaluating how to scale them profitably in multiple urban areas.

items.title: How frontier AI is rewriting software security rules
items.desc: As AI makes it easier and faster for cyberattackers to discover and exploit vulnerabilities in software, companies must change their approach to safeguarding their digital assets and infrastructure.

items.title: Turning executive judgment into organizational intelligence: Leveraging AI in CEO leadership
items.desc: The judgment of the CEO and top leaders is one of the most valuable sources of knowledge in the organization. AI can now codify that tacit wisdom and make it available to everyone, for the first time.

items.title: Critical infrastructure is under threat. Are organizations prepared?
items.desc: Organizations may not recognize their exposure to conventional, cyber, and hybrid risks until a disruption occurs. Here is how they can anticipate and reduce risks associated with these threats.

items.title: Wärtsilä CEO Håkan Agnevall: Focus, flexibility, and the next wave of growth
items.desc: Industrial leaders can turn disruption into growth by sharpening their focus, scaling to meet surging data-center power demand, and putting AI and continuous improvement to work.

items.title: Overcoming the R&D bottleneck: Building a causal decision system
items.desc: Tackling stalled development productivity requires sharp decision making. Leading biopharma are replacing fragmented analysis with connected, causal decision systems to optimize speed, cost, and success rates.

items.title: Closing banking’s AI value gap: A CEO guide
items.desc: As AI adoption races ahead, great value is being left behind. Leaders need an operating model that turns investment into AI capital that can be deployed again and again.

items.title: Banking on AI: How a new operating model can transform distressed credit management
items.desc: Banks increasingly deploy AI in distressed credit management. But few have adjusted their operating models to deliver distinctive customer experiences and optimize financial outcomes and recovery costs.

items.title: Agentic AI in strategic sourcing: Hype or hero?
items.desc: As more procurement functions invest in agentic AI to capture savings and drive efficiency, the question is increasingly: Is it worth it?

items.title: Rewiring securities services for a new era of competition and growth
items.desc: Disruptive forces—from real-time settlement to agentic AI—are changing the dynamics of the securities services industry. How can leaders capture the next horizon of growth?

items.title: What AI can’t replace—and why it matters for value
items.desc: AI may be deepening our crisis of connection, says Stanford research psychologist Jamil Zaki. Managing change with empathy helps leaders build trust, strengthen relationships, and get the most out of their AI investments.

items.title: The rise of the agentic coworker: A banking CIO’s guide to the next wave of AI
items.desc: AI agents can increasingly make decisions, act, and collaborate across workflows. Deploying them at scale requires new approaches to governance, architecture, and accountability.

items.title: Pfizer’s Alex Condoleon on medical affairs accountability
items.desc: Pfizer’s chief medical affairs officer talks about measuring medical affairs’ true impact, leading change at scale, and what patient-first really means.

items.title: Agentic AI in financial-crime prevention: Lessons from winners
items.desc: A year of delivery has confirmed much of what we expected about agentic AI in financial-crime prevention—and inspired five key questions that can help institutions scale.

items.title: Agentic AI in transaction monitoring: How banks can scale AI in compliance
items.desc: Applying AI to transaction monitoring shows how agents can transform compliance tasks and processes, turning cost centers into drivers of advantage.

items.title: Author Talks: AI is advancing. Is our judgment keeping up?
items.desc: Can we unlock AI’s promise without surrendering human judgment? Technology leader Tiffany Xingyu Wang says the answer lies in learning not whether to trust AI, but when—and how much.

items.title: Three horizons of quantum: A business road map to the future computing economy
items.desc: In the next decade, quantum technology could create trillions in value and break encryption, delivering opportunity but also risk. Leading companies are acting now to secure a competitive advantage.

items.title: Securing software in the age of AI: Red Hat CTO Chris Wright
items.desc: Open-source veteran Chris Wright explains why AI-driven vulnerability discovery is forcing a reckoning for software security, and how the industry can emerge stronger as a result.

items.title: The next era of US retirement: Four shifts redefining competition
items.desc: The US retirement industry is entering a new era. Four shifts, from AI to product innovation, are redefining where value will be created.

items.title: Getting real about AI: How AI agents are changing the economics of software engineering
items.desc: Cognition co-founder and President Russell Kaplan explains why the next frontier of AI in software engineering is about more than writing code faster and what it takes to turn autonomous agents into measurable business value.

items.title: What is a forward-deployed engineer?
items.desc: Forward-deployed engineers work inside another company’s own systems. Three McKinsey leaders explain how FDEs help companies derive impact from AI.

items.title: The judgment bottleneck: Balancing AI and human speeds in strategy
items.desc: Analysis now runs on AI time, but judgment still runs on human time. Three moves can help turn AI’s speed into better strategy decisions.

items.title: Strengthening supply chains behind US semiconductors
items.desc: New research maps hidden upstream dependencies in the US semiconductor supply chain and outlines potential mitigation strategies to make the ecosystem more resilient.

items.title: Voices on Planning: The AI-powered future of supply chain
items.desc: The shift from software as a service to AI-enabled planning could move decision-making from fixed cycles to real time, but success will require the right governance, expertise, and operating model.

items.title: The AI value curve: The economics of applying AI to existing work
items.desc: Many organizations are still measuring AI adoption instead of value. The AI value curve helps identify where AI’s automation potential can be deployed most cost-effectively.

items.title: Rewiring capital projects to boost construction productivity
items.desc: McKinsey’s Capital Excellence experts discuss how AI and technology can boost construction productivity, address labor shortages, and accelerate delivery of complex capital projects.

items.title: What does AI really cost?
items.desc: Moving an AI tool from pilot to production can nearly quadruple its cost. Three McKinsey experts explain why—and how to tell whether it’s worth it.

items.title: Why the future of capital projects belongs to digital and AI-enabled teams
items.desc: Digital and AI are changing the way capital projects are selected, designed, procured, built, and steered. Leaders are moving beyond pilots to rewire how projects are planned and delivered.

items.title: The AI operating system: A new way for CEOs to run the enterprise
items.desc: An AI operating system can become an enterprise’s “second brain,” but only if CEOs rethink how management itself evolves.

items.title: McKinsey research shows AI creating more jobs than automation displaces — but 11 million American workers will need help this decade
items.desc: While debates about AI’s impact on the workforce dominate headlines, the biggest challenge ahead will be helping workers find the most direct pathway into growing jobs, write Eric Kutcher and Tanguy Catlin in Fortune.

items.title: As the world order turns, leading companies are keeping pace. Here’s how
items.desc: Leading companies are tracking six emerging patterns of geopolitical change and realigning their businesses to achieve resilience, seize growth, and build competitive advantage.

items.title: Why AI’s easiest wins are misleading CEOs
AI is changing work. Now it has to change the organization
items.desc: The first phase of enterprise AI put powerful new tools in people’s hands. Capturing the larger opportunity from agentic AI will require leaders to rethink the shape of the organization itself.

items.title: Scaling AI inference
items.desc: Inference is reshaping AI economics, infrastructure architectures, and investment priorities across the semiconductor ecosystem.

items.title: Pause, pivot, or accelerate: SaaS in the age of agentic AI
items.desc: Agentic AI is reshaping the case for modernization in insurance. Leaders from Guidewire, Bessemer Venture Partners, and SAP discuss how insurers can respond, considering their existing commitments.

items.title: Siemens’s next reinvention: An interview with Cedrik Neike
items.desc: As technology transforms the factory floor, industrial companies are confronting a broader question: What will it take to lead the next era of manufacturing?

items.title: The bank’s digital twin: The future of nonfinancial risk management
items.desc: The risk function’s fundamental purpose has not changed, but the nature of the risks, the pace at which they materialize, and the tools available to manage them have.

items.title: Modernizing for the mission: An interview with Jamie Wolff
items.desc: The National Nuclear Security Administration’s CIO shares that modernization means rebuilding infrastructure, data, and talent at once—while keeping the mission and a relentless pace of change in mind.

items.title: The CEO’s singular impact on the success—or failure—of AI in organizations
items.desc: There are certain aspects of the AI opportunity that chief executives cannot hand off to others—raising the organization’s ambition, rearchitecting how it works, and resetting its culture.

items.title: Workforce in motion: Skills and pathways to future jobs in the United States
items.desc: AI, automation, and broader structural trends are accelerating the reallocation of work across the US economy. Capturing its benefits requires developing new professional pathways and skills, and reducing barriers between declining and growing occupations.

items.title: The next phase of government AI economics
items.desc: Subsidized AI pilots are expiring as usage explodes. Here’s how US public sector leaders can treat AI spend as a managed category before the bill arrives.

items.title: Make life better: Mikhail Lomtadze’s customer-first philosophy
items.desc: Mikhail Lomtadze, cofounder and CEO of Kaspi, believes the only measure that matters is whether Kaspi makes customers’ lives better or not—and why that single conviction changes everything else.

items.title: AI is changing how we work. Is your organization ready?
items.desc: As AI reshapes roles, leaders face a bigger question: how to rethink jobs, teams, and the way work gets done in a fundamentally different era.

items.title: The AI-powered future of care
items.desc: AI won’t replace clinicians, but it can improve quality, increase access, and reshape the workforce, payments, and patient volumes. Today, AI can perform some 16 to 22 percent of US outpatient care.

items.title: Democratized superintelligence is coming: The world needs to get ready
items.desc: Bret Taylor, Sierra cofounder and OpenAI chair, believes AI’s near-term cybersecurity risks are real but solvable, and its greater power lies in delivering the world’s best knowledge to everyone.

items.title: Harnessing AI to make mining safer
items.desc: AI could improve both safety and productivity by anticipating problems before they arise, detecting worker fatigue, and automating dangerous tasks.

items.title: Maintenance meets AI: A proven approach for asset-heavy industries
items.desc: Embedding the latest AI and technology within day-to-day operations is transforming maintenance from a cost center into a significant driver of value.

items.title: India’s new insurance track: The marathon becomes an AI-led decathlon
items.desc: As India’s economy continues to ramp up, insurers have an opportunity to capture value by improving productivity, modernizing operating models, and scaling technology and AI across the enterprise.

items.title: Rewiring procurement in resources: Making judgment an enduring asset
items.desc: For procurement leaders in the resources sector, using AI to codify the function’s category expertise does not just capture more value—it turns hard-won judgment into a compounded, durable advantage.

items.title: Ready to ramp? How US manufacturers can scale at pace
items.desc: US manufacturers have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to reshore the production of critical and at-risk goods, but to do so, they will need to aggressively ramp up production from today’s levels.

items.title: WIRED: The AI playbook top companies use
items.desc: WIRED’s Katie Drummond talks with McKinsey’s Dan Swan about why capturing AI’s full potential requires companies to move beyond experimentation and fundamentally rewire their businesses.

items.title: The economics of AI
items.desc: AI is getting more expensive for companies. As rising token usage and workflow complexity make costs harder to predict, leaders need new ways to manage AI economics.

items.title: Could aviation at last be close to earning its wings?
items.desc: The aviation value chain’s recent performance tells divergent stories: More airlines are creating value, and more are doing so consistently—yet the industry still cannot cover its cost of capital.

items.title: Beauty, redefined
items.desc: Beauty now stretches from skin care to saunas, from downtown department stores to K-beauty reels. Here’s what these shifts mean for brands seeking to connect with consumers.

items.title: Rethinking growth with AI: A conversation with Slack CMO Ryan Gavin
items.desc: At Cannes Lions 2026, Slack CMO Ryan Gavin and McKinsey Partner Jeff Jacobs discussed how AI can turn productivity gains into a lever for growth.

items.title: Why growth and specialization matter more than ever in private equity
items.desc: Creating value in private equity increasingly depends on transforming businesses, growing them profitably, and building operational excellence, as Providence Equity Partners has learned firsthand.

items.title: Advancing adaptation: Breaking barriers to a trillion-dollar opportunity
items.desc: Climate adaptation delivers benefits far greater than its costs, but investment lags. What are the barriers to scaling adaptation and how could they be overcome?

items.title: Future of Wellness 2027: Inside the $2.7 trillion takeover
items.desc: More consumers are prioritizing their health and scrutinizing what they buy. Our latest Future of Wellness research explores the trends shaping where they spend and what they expect in return.

items.title: Who wins when AI does the shopping? New evidence on agentic commerce
items.desc: Analysis of about 21,000 consumers indicates how AI shopping behavior is growing and evolving, with early evidence showing companies are not yet equipped to meet the rising demand.

items.title: The State of Grocery Retail Europe: Implications for packaging players
items.desc: Continued growth pressure on European grocery retailers limits opportunities for packaging players. In this environment, cost competitiveness remains imperative.

items.title: Focus, scale, fund: The AI playbook CPG leaders are missing

items.title: 美股波動持續放大，短線避險情緒增溫
items.body: VIX近5日增加1.42至22.57，VVIX也升至112.81。SKEW上升2.8%達153.55，指標顯示市場波動放大的現象正在持續。

items.title: 原油運費雙雙回檔，進口成本壓力趨緩
items.body: WTI原油跌3.59%至87.57美元，Brent原油跌4.33%至94.06美元。 Drewry WCI一週下跌1.0%至4389.0美元，上海到紐約運費降幅達3.0%。

items.title: CPI年增率下降與失業率微降
items.body: 10月CPI年增率降至2.33%、核心CPI年增率降至2.23%，9月失業率降至3.36%。

items.title: 信用卡簽帳總額成長
items.body: 8月信用卡總計簽帳金額達3269.0億元，年增9.9%。

items.title: 外銷熱與實體零售衰退並存
items.body: 外銷訂單年增62.4%、燈號紅燈41分，但批發零售淨減118家，百貨刷卡比整體慢3.9個百分點。

items.title: 桃園人口淨遷入居冠
items.body: 桃園市單月淨遷入達1060人，為全台各縣市中最高，金門縣次之達320人。

items.title: 新設公司淨增加數縮水，創3年新低
items.body: 2026年9月新設公司2909家、解散2355家，淨增加2107家。跟去年同期的淨增加3302家相比顯著減少，新設公司3年變動率為-10.0%。

items.title: 機械維修與家具製造業翻轉呈淨增加
items.body: 2026年8月產業用機械設備維修及安裝業淨增加12家，遠高於上月的-13家；家具製造業淨增加7家，亦高於上月的-2家，逆勢轉正。

items.title: 標案現運動與設備採購需求
items.body: 115年度政府標案出現多項運動設施及採購需求，包含宜蘭縣凱旋國小10377124元工程標案，以及虎尾科大3527000元的肌骨動態模擬系統案。

items.title: 輝達執行長遭調查衝擊供應鏈
items.body: 美國華盛頓消息指川普稱聯邦調查局正調查輝達執行長與疑似中國間諜的婚外情，此事件關聯度達4，直接牽動台灣半導體供應鏈神經與相關個股走勢。

items.title: 網路謠言未查核比例高達八成
items.body: LINE流傳訊息偏向負面情緒（分數-0.3），查核平台資料顯示熱門舉報有25件，其中20件尚未查核、3件為謠言，通報總次數達63次，顯見不實訊息正大量散布。

items.title: 共機今日全面消失 海空動態現罕見異常
items.body: 共機今日出動 0 架次，遠低於 7 日平均的 15.7 架次與 30 日平均的 10.3 架次；共艦則維持在 7 艘。

weekly.headline: 外需景氣紅燈高掛，民間消費分化收縮，銀髮寵物商機持續浮現

dirs.t: 外需極熱內需實體零售偏弱
dirs.why: 外銷訂單年增62.4%、燈號紅燈41分，但刷卡在百貨比整體慢3.9個百分點、衣慢2.5個百分點，批發零售淨減118家。

dirs.t: 科技資本支出與AI動能強勁
dirs.why: 上市櫃電腦設備營收年增65.4%、半導體增58.9%，美股財報AI代理詞彙增153%，開發套件astro增51個百分點。

dirs.t: 超高齡與少子化確立消費轉向
dirs.why: 65歲以上占20.7%、出生年增-11.2%，維基寵物關注度比其他主題高40個百分點，立院三讀老人福利法修正案。
src: 維基關注度（比其他主題）

gaps.t: 寵物照護與服務供給落後
gaps.why: 維基寵物比其他主題高40個百分點、媒體熱度+132，但商標-20、新店-3，寵物食品法草案也已送立法院審議。
src: 主題鏈（需求 vs 供給）
維基關注度（比其他主題）

gaps.t: 睡眠與高壓修復需求未被滿足
gaps.why: 搜尋+12、媒體+63，但相關商標-23、新店-3且消費-4，供給端與產品佈局尚未跟上公眾健康關注度。
src: 主題鏈（需求 vs 供給）
